new_statements.venue: Joint statement with Sen. John Curtis (Republican, Utah) and their letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick, Senate press release
new_statements.quote: Our concerns about insufficient export controls on these technologies are magnified by numerous rogue artificial intelligence incidents, including autonomous hacking incidents, unauthorized agent access to the internet, and attacks on real-world targets.
new_statements.context: The two senators urged tighter export controls on advanced AI chips to China; they continue that these incidents show the urgent need to protect the safety and security of Americans, and that company whistleblowers have warned the technology is accelerating without sufficient guardrails.
new_statements.reason: Points to rogue, autonomous AI incidents as a reason for concern and (in the next passage) a threat to the safety and security of Americans, a serious but general threat; the harms named are hacking and attacks, so it sits near D under the rogue-AI ruling.

new_record_items: With Sen. John Curtis, sent a letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick urging him to close loopholes in export controls on advanced AI chips (including remote access by Chinese companies), citing rogue AI incidents and whistleblower warnings that AI is accelerating without sufficient guardrails.

Congressional delegation visit to San Francisco on national security and emerging technology, including meetings with AI experts and OpenAI leadership; her quoted remarks in the release do not mention AI risk.
grade_reason: Her 2026 letters and joint statements treat autonomous AI incidents as a severe threat to Americans' safety and say AI must remain under human control, but nothing found names mass casualties, loss of control as an outcome, or extinction. The new November 2026 letter is consistent with C.
